key_insight: Clean pages have an authoritative flash copy, so DRAM needs only detection, not correction: a CRC plus refetch turns uncorrectable errors into latency instead of data loss.
killer_doubt: At 1% BER only 0.99^512 = 0.6% of 64 B lines read clean, so nearly every access pays a ~50 us SSD refetch. With SECDED it works only below ~3e-4.
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-05038/I-01312: bitmap 200 reject-bin dies at 85 C, classify random versus clustered faults, then replay weight and page-cache traces with SECDED plus CRC-refetch to measure mean and p99 added latency against raw BER.
prior_art: Linux hwpoison already drops and re-reads clean page-cache pages on uncorrectable errors (2009); Micron SpecTek off-spec bins; EDEN approximate DRAM (MICRO 2019). From memory.

key_insight: Thermal drawing really is km/hour and litho-free, and draw-down sets layer thickness geometrically; the multimaterial-fiber toolset exists.
killer_doubt: Oxide semiconductors do not flow at glass draw temperatures, and co-drawable glassy chalcogenides leak far above the ~10 fA retention budget. Drawing replaces deposition, which is already cheap, not lithography.
decisive_experiment: University draw tower (~$150k): draw a chalcogenide-semiconductor/glass/metal laminate to 50 nm layers, then cut and contact one stack as a TFT. Measure layer continuity by TEM, Ion/Ioff and 85 C off-current; kill above 1e-13 A.
prior_art: MIT Fink and Abouraddy multimaterial fibers; in-fiber thin-film capillary breakup into filaments; R16 DROP of drawn-coax I-01820; in-batch I-11235. From memory.

key_insight: No-etch capacitor mold: etchable-core nanochannel glass with 30-50 nm pores, sliced 1-5 um and ALD-lined TiN/ZrO2/TiN, gives ~3-5 fF per um. CMOS keeps the switches.
killer_doubt: Molten metal cores break up (Rayleigh-Plateau, ~ms at 25 nm radius), forcing etchable cores. Then ~1% draw-pitch disorder misregisters 50 nm-pitch pores against transistors within ~100 cells.
decisive_experiment: Draw etchable-core nanochannel glass to 50 nm pores (~$200k), slice 2 um discs, ALD MIM-fill, and bond to a pad wafer with pads wider than pitch for registration-free contact. Measure fF/pad, leakage, shorts and open-pore yield.
prior_art: NRL nanochannel glass (Tonucci et al., Science 1992, ~33 nm channels); photonic-crystal-fiber stack-and-draw; Phase B AAO-Cap B2-01; R16 DROP I-01820. From memory.

key_insight: The recoverable helium is concentrated: an ESC patent reports ~19.5 of ~20 sccm backside helium is dumped pure through a bleed orifice, before mixing with exhaust (via search snippet).
killer_doubt: Membranes and PSA are the wrong tool: the bleed is already pure and closed-loop control removes it at source; the ~0.5 sccm past the seal dilutes to ~10-25 ppm.
decisive_experiment: Helium mass balance on one etch bay: meter supply, bleed and foreline per chuck for a week. Then retrofit a no-bleed closed-loop backside controller and report helium per wafer and wafer-temperature uniformity. ~$100k.
prior_art: Patent family 'Increasing the gas efficiency for an electrostatic chuck' (US 9753463, 11747834, 12493303) (via search snippet); commercial membrane/PSA helium recovery units.

key_insight: Same core as I-10762: H2 out-conducts He (0.18 versus 0.15 W/m-K) and can be made on site. The recycle loop into the forming-gas header is the only addition.
killer_doubt: The recycle loop is pointless and fragile: ~20 sccm per chuck is ~2.6 g H2/day (cents), cheaper than a Pd purifier, and HBr/halogen traces from chambers poison Pd membranes.
decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-10762 single-chamber trial; a separate test of the recycle loop is not warranted.
prior_art: ESC patents list hydrogen among backside cooling gases (via search snippet); Pd-membrane H2 purifiers are commercial. Duplicate of in-batch I-10762.

key_insight: H2 beats He at both limits: continuum conductivity 0.18 versus 0.15 W/m-K, and ~1.2-2x free-molecular transfer per Torr. Its higher Paschen minimum (~270 versus ~150 V) also cuts backside arcing.
killer_doubt: H2 thermal accommodation on real, film-coated wafer backsides is unmeasured (~0.1-0.3); at the low end gap transfer drops ~2x. Plus NFPA 55/SEMI S2 qualification in every chamber.
decisive_experiment: Swap He for H2 at 5-30 Torr on one 300 mm etch chamber. Map wafer temperature with thermocouple wafers under 2-5 kW bias, measure HAR oxide etch rate and selectivity drift, and log exhaust H2 against the 4% LFL. ~$300k.
prior_art: ESC patents list hydrogen beside He/Ar/N2; vendors moved to N2/Ar despite arcing limits (via search snippet). No production H2 backside use found.

key_insight: Inline compression behind CXL multiplies capacity per DRAM die without wafers, and an FPGA demo is cheap.
killer_doubt: It is already commercial. Fleet data show ~20-30% of memory cold at ~3x, a system gain of ~15-25%, not 2-3x, and it adds ~50-100 ns decompression latency.
decisive_experiment: None warranted beyond replaying public far-memory traces through LZ4/base-delta models (~$20k), as for R16 I-08737.
prior_art: ZeroPoint Technologies; Marvell Structera A inline LZ4; OCP Hyperscale CXL Tiered Memory Expander; Google zswap far memory (ASPLOS 2019). From memory.

key_insight: Bradley-Harper ripples self-organize 20-40 nm gratings in one broad-beam step, and coarse pre-patterns can phase-lock them: a cheap 1D grating source.
killer_doubt: Ripple fields carry ~1-10 line merges per um2 (~1e8/cm2, estimate) versus DSA's still-unadopted ~1/cm2, and each merge shorts a wordline. SAQP already makes DUV gratings without EUV.
decisive_experiment: Make templated Ar+ ripples on a-Si over a 1 cm2 coupon at 30 nm pitch. Count line terminations and merges by SEM over 1e4 um2 and measure LWR; proceed only below ~1e-4 defects/um2.
prior_art: Bradley-Harper theory (1988); Facsko ion-sputtered dots (1999); Cuenat-Aziz templated ripples (2005); DSA as the better-ordered benchmark. From memory.

key_insight: A write is a refresh: data provably dead or rewritten within the retention window needs none, and a write-timestamp turns that proof into a checkable fault, not silent corruption.
killer_doubt: The large footprints outlive 30 ms: KV blocks last seconds to minutes and training activations ~0.1-10 s. Refresh is only ~4-8% of active power, and row hammer still needs PRAC.
decisive_experiment: Instrument vLLM serving and a Megatron training run to log byte-weighted data lifetimes. Kill if under 10% of resident bytes die within 30 ms. ~$20k of GPU time.
prior_art: RANA refresh-optimized eDRAM DNN accelerator (ISCA 2018); Smart Refresh (MICRO 2007); ESKIMO semantic refresh (MICRO 2009); GPU eDRAM register files. From memory.

key_insight: Panel memory needs on-glass periphery. IGZO gate-driver-on-array already ships n-only bootstrapped decoders, so only the sense amps need new work, and offset cancellation can stand in for a good p-oxide.
killer_doubt: Large-area oxide-TFT Vt sigma of ~20-50 mV gives a 6-sigma sense-amp offset of 120-300 mV against a ~50-100 mV bitline signal. Displays still use silicon column drivers.
decisive_experiment: On a university or Gen-2 oxide TFT line, build 10k offset-compensated n-only latch sense amps plus a bootstrapped decoder at L=0.5-1 um. Measure offset distribution, sense time versus signal, and energy per access. ~$300k.
prior_art: IGZO gate-driver-on-array in OLED/LCD panels; SEL CAAC-IGZO NOSRAM/DOSRAM; Phase B B2-08 complementary-oxide sense amps; p-SnO/Cu2O TFT literature.

key_insight: Winding is stacking without monolithic yield loss: every web turn can be tested and mapped before winding, unlike a 20-tier stack, where one bad tier scraps the panel.
killer_doubt: Polyimide web moves ~10 ppm/K, ~100 um across 1 m per 10 K, against ~50 nm overlay needed at F=0.25 um. Edge schoopage shorts ~4,700 turns onto one bus.
decisive_experiment: Only after I-10785's rigid-glass arrays work: imprint 2-mask oxide-TFT arrays on 25 um polyimide web at 0.5 um, and measure overlay and TFT yield over 10 m of web. ~$400k.
prior_art: HP self-aligned imprint lithography (SAIL) for roll-to-roll TFTs; metallized-film capacitor schoopage; Thin Film Electronics printed memory. From memory.

key_insight: Oxide-TFT leakage makes planar caps enough: 0.25 um2 of 10 nm TiO2/Al2O3 (k~30) holds ~6 fF. 20 tiers give ~5 TB/m2 at a cost per m2 ~100-1000x below DRAM wafers.
killer_doubt: No panel tool images 0.25 um at ~50 nm overlay: FPD steppers resolve ~1.5 um with ~0.3-0.5 um overlay. And 100 patterning steps (20 tiers x 5 masks) compound defects.
decisive_experiment: Build two tiers of ZnSnO 1T1C arrays at F=0.25 um on 200 mm glass with a commercial step-and-repeat imprinter. Measure overlay, killer defects/cm2 per mask, Vt sigma and 85 C retention, then feed a panel-maker cost-per-mask-m2 model. ~$600k.
prior_art: Phase B B2-19 panel 3D oxide memory; SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM; R16 DROP of 2 um display-glass memory (I-03879); Canon NIL; large-area wire-grid imprint.
